item.title: Urban Planning Principles of Harappa
item.explanation: Harappan cities demonstrated advanced urban planning: grid-pattern streets, sub-surface covered brick drainage systems, standardized baked bricks, and public baths.
item.source_context: Chapter 6: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation (fees106.pdf)

item.statement: The Harappan civilisation flourished during its urban mature phase between 2600 BCE and 1900 BCE.

item.name: Lothal
item.significance: Harappan port city in Gujarat featuring the world's earliest known artificial tidal brick dockyard.

item.name: Mohenjo-daro

item.name: Dholavira
item.significance: Harappan city in Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, famous for its sophisticated water reservoirs and three-tier city planning.

item.historical_significance: Flourishing mature period of planned cities, metal craftsmanship, dockyards, and international trade in northwestern South Asia.
item.source_context: Chapter 6: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation (fees106.pdf)

stages: 1. Early Phase: Agricultural settlement expansion and copper metalwork development.
2. Mature Phase (2600–1900 BCE): Flourishing urbanism with brick architecture, grid streets, and global maritime trade.
3. Late / De-urbanisation Phase (post-1900 BCE): River course changes and climate shifts lead to rural migration.
item.source_context: Chapter 6: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation (fees106.pdf)
